Maximal oxygen uptake and long-distance running performance

Maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max) is the maximum amount of oxygen that can be consumed per unit of body weight per unit of time (ml/kg/min), and it often appears as a performance indicator for long-distance athletes.
The average value for a 30-year-old male is around 40 ml/kg/min per body weight, but the VO2max of elite long-distance runners is said to reach as high as 90 ml/kg/min (
). It is known that there is a relationship between VO2max and running ability across various levels of runners, as shown below.
